question: Do matched WebArena-Verified task families with controlled novelty fraction (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% unseen identifiers, training on resource A testing on never-observed B) show later-agent cost (tokens, browser calls, latency, retrieval+verification+repair amortized over frequency) tracking residual novelty rather than full task length when SPIDER parameterized inheritance (with freshness gating and UNKNOWN abstention) is compared vs COLD vs instructions vs retrieval/RAG vs TERX/BrowserBash 0-token replay + LLM fallback strong baselines?
hypothesis: Later-agent cost under SPIDER parameterized inheritance with freshness gating and UNKNOWN abstention tracks residual novelty fraction, not full task length: cost_SPIDER(novelty) = C_fixed (retrieval+verification) + C_novel * novelty_fraction where C_fixed is low constant (~retrieval+verify) and C_novel << C_cold_full. At 0% novelty (all identifiers seen during training on resource A, test uses same identifiers), SPIDER cost is << COLD cost (>=60% reduction, near 0-token REPLAY cost) with high reuse fraction >=0.90. At 100% novelty (all identifiers unseen, never-observed B), SPIDER cost via UNKNOWN fallback ≈ COLD cost (not more than 10% higher) with false_accept <=0.10. Spearman rho(cost_SPIDER, novelty_fraction) >=0.60 (p<0.01) and novelty-fraction model R2 exceeds full-task-length model R2 by >=0.15. SPIDER amortized cost per success (including retrieval+verification+repair over repeat frequency f=1,10,100) beats B-COLD, B-RAG, and B-INSTRUCTIONS at low novelty (0%,25%) and beats B-REPLAY-TERX at any novelty >0% where exact replay fails, demonstrating pay-cost-of-novelty work compression.
falsifier: FALSIFIED if ANY of: (F1) SPIDER success <0.85 at 0% novelty or <0.70 averaged across bins with false_accept >0.10 (parameterized inheritance does not work even on seen identifiers or contaminates via false accepts); (F2) SPIDER amortized cost at 0% novelty not meaningfully cheaper than B-COLD (ratio SPIDER/COLD >0.65) or SPIDER 0% cost >3x B-REPLAY-TERX (no advantage over strong replay baseline for exact repeats); (F3) No novelty tracking: Spearman rho(cost_SPIDER, novelty) <0.35 or p>=0.05 or slope not >0, indicating cost does not increase with novelty; (F4) Novelty does not explain cost better than full length: R2_novelty - R2_full_length <0.05 (and full_length is constant by design, so failure means cost flat or driven by other factors); (F5) SPIDER not beating B-RAG retrieval baseline at low novelty (SPIDER amortized cost >= B-RAG cost at 0% and 25%), meaning parameterized inheritance adds no value beyond nearest-trajectory retrieval; (F6) Positive controls fail (exact-repeat literal replay not 0-token, or training-resource-A tested on same A fails) or null controls show spurious novelty tracking (shuffled mapping rho >=0.35). MIXED if C1 (success+low false_accept) passes but F3/F4 fail: mechanisms work but cost is flat (constant overhead) rather than residual-novelty-proportional, implying reuse without compression. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if harness cannot bind parameters, browser/call simulation broken, or all conditions <0.50 success even at 0% (substrate failure, not scientific falsification).

baselines.description: Cold start with no SPIDER memory: simulated LLM explores task from scratch each time. Cost = full task length * simulated LLM cost (500 tokens/step + 2 browser calls/step + 120ms browser latency). No retrieval, no verification, no reuse. Represents upper bound full-length cost.
baselines.expected: Cost independent of novelty fraction (flat line ~ task_length * unit_cost). Success rate measured but expected lower than SPIDER with inheritance. Used as denominator for work-compression ratio.

baselines.description: Site-specific hand-authored instructions baseline (strong instruction prompt, no retrieval). Simulates providing the agent with natural-language site instructions (e.g., catalog search procedure) but no parameterized mechanism. Cost = instruction tokens (amortized) + full exploration of identifier-specific steps. Tests whether instructions alone achieve novelty-proportional cost without SPIDER.
baselines.expected: Cost slightly below B-COLD but still ~ full length; not novelty-proportional beyond instruction token savings. Expected to be beaten by SPIDER at low novelty by >=15% amortized.

baselines.description: Semantic retrieval / RAG over prior trajectories: nearest successful trajectory retrieved by token-overlap / embedding similarity (simulated via Jaccard over intent+keywords), replayed verbatim without parameter induction. If retrieved trajectory identifiers match test identifiers exactly, reuse is exact; otherwise replay fails and falls back to B-COLD LLM exploration for mismatched steps. Strong memory baseline that beats weak memory; per ARCHITECTURE memory-vs-memory requirement.
baselines.expected: Cost = retrieval cost (150ms + 200 tokens) + exact-match reuse where identifiers overlap + fallback LLM cost for mismatched steps. At 0% novelty should be similar to SPIDER; at >=25% novelty should be worse than SPIDER because without parameterization every novel identifier triggers full fallback. SPIDER expected to beat B-RAG by >=20% at 0% and 25% amortized.

baselines.description: TERX / BrowserBash / HyperAgent 0-token exact replay with LLM fallback: if test task's full identifier sequence exactly equals a training trajectory, replay at 0 LLM tokens + 1 verification browser call (~90ms, per Scout external framing); otherwise replay fails (FA) and falls back to B-COLD LLM exploration for full task. This is the strongest exact-repeat economics baseline (23k->0 tokens, 173x speedup, 90ms). Tests caching vs semantic generalization tension prior: SPIDER should match REPLAY at 0% but beat it at any novelty >0%.
baselines.expected: Amortized cost = (hit_rate * 90ms + miss_rate * COLD_cost). At 0% novelty hit_rate=1.0 => cost ~90ms << SPIDER (SPIDER allowed up to 2x REPLAY at 0%). At 100% novelty hit_rate=0.0 => cost = COLD. SPIDER expected cheaper than REPLAY at 25%,50%,75%,100% where replay misses.

positive_control.description: Two positive controls: (PC1) Exact-repeat literal mechanism: training resource A mechanism replayed on same resource A with 0% novelty should achieve 100% success, reused_actions >=0.95, and TERX baseline 0 LLM tokens + 1 browser verification call. Validates substrate can measure 0-cost case. (PC2) Parameterized inheritance on seen identifiers: SPIDER distill_parameterized trained on 5 observations of resource A (e.g., SKUs A1..A5) tested on same set A should resolve EXECUTABLE with correct bound_action binding and 100% success, confirming parameter induction works before testing generalization to B.
positive_control.expected_behavior: PC1: B-REPLAY-TERX at 0% cost = 0 tokens, ~90ms, 100% success. PC2: SPIDER at 0% success >=0.95, reused_actions >=0.90, false_accept 0.0. Failure of either indicates substrate broken -> MEASUREMENT_INVALID.

null_control.description: Two null controls: (NC1) Shuffled parameter-slot mapping: randomly permute the learned parameter slot -> identifier binding (e.g., swap ${sku} with ${category}) before SPIDER resolve on same 0-100% novelty tasks. Expected: Spearman rho(cost_shuffled, novelty) |rho|<0.25 p>=0.05 and success collapses to ≤ B-COLD success, false_accept rises, proving observed novelty tracking requires correct parameterization not any reuse. (NC2) Random mechanism selection: SPIDER retrieval returns random registry entry instead of ranked match, with UNKNOWN disabled. Expected: cost flat vs novelty, no R2 advantage, false_accept >=0.30, demonstrating ranking/gating matters.
null_control.expected_behavior: NC1 rho |rho|<0.25 non-significant, NC2 false_accept >=0.30. If NC1 shows rho>=0.35 significant, observed effect is spurious (e.g., task difficulty confounded with novelty label) -> measurement invalid for novelty claim.

measurement_validity: 1. No real LLM API calls: all LLM cost is via deterministic token-count proxy (500 tokens per novel reasoning step, 50 tokens per verification step, 0 tokens for reused verified steps) and browser-call proxy (1 call per novel step = 120ms + 1 verification call per task). This bypasses the 2 LLM-key MEASUREMENT_INVALID failures flagged in Director rationale while preserving relative economics. Proxy values are frozen before execution and disclosed as assumption; sensitivity analysis varies tokens/step ±50% in report.

2. Matched task families with constant full length: each task family has fixed length L=10 steps (search->filter->open->select->add->checkout->verify) so full_task_length is constant across novelty bins; only residual_novelty_fraction varies (0%,25%,50%,75%,100% of parameterizable identifier slots are unseen B values, others are seen A values). This isolates novelty as the only varying cost driver. 20 tasks per bin = 100 SPIDER test tasks (+ same 100 for each baseline = 500 trials total). Training uses disjoint resource A SKU set (e.g., A_SKU_001..A_SKU_050); testing on resource B SKU set (B_SKU_001..B_SKU_050) with zero overlap except as controlled by novelty fraction.

3. WebArena-Verified task family source: use WebArena-Verified shopping task definitions as design template. If WebArena JSON fixtures are accessible locally (e.g., cached under /tmp or repo fixture), import task intents and accessibility-tree fragments directly; otherwise use synthetic Flask catalog mock that replicates WebArena structure (12 store instances sharing platform per EXP-INTEL-35651934683 M1=1.0, same as WebArena shopping 996 tasks). Either source satisfies the Director's 'WebArena-Verified families' strategic question while avoiding Docker-hosting dependency; the chosen source is logged in provenance.json and disclosed as validity caveat.

4. SPIDER mechanism implementation: harness-level distill_parameterized with _extract_varying_values logic (validated in EXP-PRODUCT-33741671686 but not yet kernel-integrated per audit) applied to 5 training observations per family to induce parameter_slots (e.g., ${sku}, ${store_id}). Registry stores one parameterized mechanism per family at confidence 0.90. At resolve time, require exact required_slots in params, freshness gating (behavioral_score <0.25 via JWT mock probe as in EXP-PRODUCT-35697049382, but here structural noise is catalog drift), and UNKNOWN abstention if confidence <0.80 or freshness stale. If UNKNOWN, fallback cost = B-COLD cost (honest abstention, not false accept).

5. End-to-end cost accounting: per-task cost = retrieval_cost (200 tokens + 150ms) + verification_cost (50 tokens + 120ms verification call if EXECUTABLE) + execution_cost (0 tokens for reused steps that verify, 500 tokens + 2 browser calls per novel step) + repair_cost (if verification fails, 1 additional LLM step 500 tokens + 2 calls). Amortized cost per success = total_cost / success_rate, reported at repeat frequencies f=1 (single use), f=10, f=100 (amortizing retrieval+distillation over uses) to compare vs TERX amortized 0-token replay. This satisfies Director's caching vs generalization amortization requirement.

6. Strong baseline execution: all baselines run on identical 100-task novelty-matched set with identical proxy costs and same fallback logic. B-RAG retrieval uses Jaccard over intent+keywords (TAU=0.30 as in pre-2.0 Graph). B-REPLAY-TERX uses exact action_template string equality (no parameterization) to decide hit/miss, then LLM fallback. No baseline is given privileged information.

7. Statistics: primary novelty-tracking test is Spearman rho between per-task SPIDER token cost and novelty_fraction (n=100). Power >0.90 to detect rho>=0.60 at alpha=0.01 (requires n>=44). Linear regression cost ~ novelty_fraction reports slope, p, R2_novelty. Comparison to full-length model uses ANCOVA: since length constant, test reduces to showing cost~novelty R2 >0.30 while cost~length correlation |r|<0.15 (trivially true if length constant but reported for completeness). Bootstrap 5000 resamples stratified by novelty bin for CI on cost ratios and rho. Two-sided tests.

8. Human-readable prereg frozen before any outcome-bearing measurement; code, fixtures, proxy constants, and decision thresholds are hashed in freeze.json. Execution uses deterministic seeds (Python hash randomization disabled via PYTHONHASHSEED=0, explicit random.seed(42)).
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of (C1)-(C6): (C1) SPIDER success >=0.85 at 0% novelty (Wilson 95% CI lower >=0.72) and mean success across 0-100% bins >=0.80, with false_accept_rate <=0.10 across all bins (false_accept = EXECUTABLE on wrong binding that fails verification). (C2) Work compression at low novelty: SPIDER amortized cost per success at 0% novelty <=0.35 * B-COLD cost at 0% (i.e., >=65% cheaper) at f=1, and SPIDER 0% amortized cost <=2.0 * B-REPLAY-TERX 0% cost (within 2x of 0-token replay; equality not required). At 100% novelty SPIDER/ COLD cost ratio <=1.10 (not more expensive than cold when all novel, via UNKNOWN fallback). (C3) Novelty tracking: Spearman rho(cost_SPIDER_tokens, novelty_fraction) >=0.60 with two-sided p<0.01 and 95% bootstrap CI lower >0.35, slope >0 p<0.01. (C4) Residual-novelty explanatory power: R2_novelty - R2_full_length >=0.15 where R2_novelty is from linear regression cost ~ novelty_fraction, R2_full_length from cost ~ full_task_length (length constant 10, so R2_full_length expected ~0.00; report difference). If task length truly constant, pass requires R2_novelty >=0.30. (C5) Beating strong memory baselines: SPIDER amortized cost per success beats B-RAG by >=20% at both 0% and 25% bins (cost_SPIDER / cost_RAG <=0.80) at f=10 amortized, and beats B-INSTRUCTIONS by >=15% at same bins (<=0.85). Additionally SPIDER beats B-REPLAY-TERX at any novelty >=25% (cost_SPIDER < cost_REPLAY at 25%,50%,75%,100% bins, each at f=10). (C6) Controls: PC1 REPLAY 0% cost =0 LLM tokens (verified) and PC2 SPIDER 0% reused_actions >=0.90 pass; NC1 shuffled rho |rho|<0.25 p>=0.05 and NC2 random retrieval false_accept >=0.30 (or rho |rho|<0.25). FALSIFIED if any C1-C6 fails (excluding PC/NC substrate failures which are MEASUREMENT_INVALID). MIXED if C1 passes but C3 or C4 fails: mechanisms succeed but cost is flat (constant overhead, no proportionality), indicating reuse without compression. MEASUREMENT_INVALID if PC1/PC2 fail (<0.50 success even at 0% for all systems) or harness cannot bind/execute parameterized mechanisms (binding error rate >0.20), or NC1 spuriously shows rho>=0.35 (confounding). Audit must recompute rho, R2, cost ratios from raw per-task CSV.
product_consequence_positive: If SURVIVES: C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY advances from HYPOTHESIS to EXPERIMENTAL (bounded: synthetic/WebArena-inspired catalog mock, L=10 fixed, token/browser proxy, localhost Flask or cached JSON, n=100). Establishes first direct evidence that later-agent cost tracks residual novelty not full length, with quantified compression (≥65% cheaper than COLD at 0%, novelty R2 advantage ≥0.15, beats RAG and REPLAY at >0%). This unblocks C-PRODUCT-ECON: provides the residual-novelty effect size needed to justify amortized-economics scale-up with real LLM measurement and Docker full-DOM hosting (Intel sample-level overlap + Runtime distributed replication become next prerequisites). Product can justify SPIDER parameterized inheritance as commercial viability lever despite TERX 90ms 0-token exact-repeat advantage. No immediate PRODUCT_CORE promotion; requires replication with real LLM tokens and production WebArena hosting.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIED: C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY remains HYPOTHESIS (or bounded REJECTED for proxy setting: cost flat or not cheaper than strong baselines). If cost flat despite success (MIXED), product must investigate constant overhead (retrieval/verification not amortized, or repair cost dominates) rather than residual-novelty scaling. If SPIDER not beating B-RAG/REPLAY, parameterized inheritance adds no economics beyond retrieval or exact replay, supporting the caching-vs-generalization tension prior that exact replay dominates at current scale and SPIDER needs different leverage (e.g., C-FRESHNESS freshness guards, C-DELTA-REPAIR, or C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE). If MEASUREMENT_INVALID due to harness/binding failures, priority is fixing distill_parameterized kernel integration (prior FALSIFIED filters) before re-testing economics. Either negative outcome redirects Product lane to higher-leverage claims and prevents premature C-PRODUCT-ECON scale-up.
estimated_cost: Zero LLM API calls (token proxy). Synthetic Flask catalog mock or cached WebArena JSON fixtures. ~800 lines Python (harness + mock server if needed). 5 novelty bins *20 tasks *5 conditions (COLD/INSTRUCTIONS/RAG/REPLAY/SPIDER) + 2 controls *100 = ~700 task trials. Each trial simulated (no real browser): ~2ms per trial. Total wall-clock <10 minutes on GitHub Actions runner. No Docker, no external APIs, no browser automation required. Storage: per-task CSV ~700 rows + registry JSON.
expected_information_gain: HIGH: This is the first direct measurement of SPIDER's central economic hypothesis after one inflated doc survey (M1 0.818->0.311, no cost measurement). Either a positive (novelty-proportional compression beating strong replay/RAG baselines) or a valid negative (flat cost or no advantage over RAG/REPLAY) decisively changes a product decision: (1) whether C-PRODUCT-ECON amortized economics scale-up is justified vs premature, (2) whether parameterized inheritance justifies productization despite TERX 0-token exact-repeat dominance, (3) whether the caching vs generalization tradeoff favors SPIDER at low-to-moderate novelty. Resolves the Director's flagged opportunity cost of 10+ narrow DGP experiments on same synthetic loops. Informs Global Director's next allocation across C-DELTA-REPAIR, C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE, and real-LLM C-LLM-INHERIT.
